reviewerNote: Second scene of the class the reporter hit: display lettering over flat saturated colour, opened as a standalone image. One line of red Cyrillic display type over a pale blue-grey ground, and the app produces no plate at all on it today (converted 2026-08-12 with -ocr -ocr-lang rus: the page carries the picture and nothing else), which is the same failure as poster-display-type-on-flat-colour and is why it is annotated. Line geometry measured from the pixels by luminance threshold (lum < 150) and projection; the same band at lum < 120 moves by at most one pixel, so the box does not depend on the cut-off. Transcript read from the image by eye. Scene ambiguity is partly-illegible, not clear, for one reason recorded rather than hidden: two printer credits sit at the foot of the poster and are visible as marks but not resolvable as glyphs at this scan resolution - at lum < 170 they do not separate from the ground at all and at lum < 190 the ground itself becomes ink, so no honest box can be measured for them. They are therefore not annotated, and a plate landing on them will count as an unmatched plate on this scene.
